requirements.summary: A Data Analyst at a Bay Area B2B SaaS company writes SQL against a cloud warehouse to answer questions about pipeline, funnel conversion, retention, product usage and revenue, then publishes the results as BI dashboards and short written analyses for go-to-market, product and finance teams. People get hired mainly by passing a live or take-home SQL test (joins, aggregations, window functions) and by showing they can turn messy SaaS data into a clear, correct metric and recommendation. Knowledge of SaaS metrics and CRM/marketing data helps set candidates apart.

skills.name: SQL querying: joins, aggregations, CTEs, subqueries and window functions
skills.howEmployersCheck: Live SQL screen (CoderPad, HackerRank or shared editor) or timed take-home against a sample schema, often with funnel or retention questions

skills.name: BI dashboard building (Tableau, Looker, Power BI, Mode or Sigma)
skills.howEmployersCheck: Portfolio dashboard review, or a take-home that asks for a visualization plus a walkthrough in the interview

skills.name: SaaS business metrics: ARR/MRR, churn, net and gross revenue retention, CAC, LTV, pipeline and funnel conversion
skills.howEmployersCheck: Case or business-sense interview questions, e.g. 'how would you define and calculate churn for us' or 'why did pipeline drop this quarter'

skills.name: Analytical problem framing and metric definition
skills.howEmployersCheck: Product/business case interview where the candidate turns a vague question into metrics, data sources and an analysis plan

skills.name: Data cleaning and validation: deduplication, null handling, reconciling numbers across sources
skills.howEmployersCheck: Take-home with deliberately messy data; interview questions about how you QA a number before sharing it

skills.name: Presenting findings to non-technical stakeholders
skills.howEmployersCheck: Presentation of the take-home or a past project to a panel; behavioral questions about influencing a decision with data

skills.name: Advanced spreadsheets: pivots, lookups (XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH), quick ad hoc models
skills.howEmployersCheck: Usually assumed from experience; sometimes part of a take-home exercise

skills.name: CRM and marketing automation data models (Salesforce objects, HubSpot/Marketo), attribution and lead-to-revenue funnel
skills.howEmployersCheck: Interview discussion of how leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities and campaigns relate; essential for GTM/revenue analytics roles

skills.name: Cloud data warehouse familiarity (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift or Databricks)
skills.howEmployersCheck: Resume keywords and interview questions on warehouse concepts, schemas and query cost/performance

skills.name: Python for analysis (pandas, notebooks) or R
skills.howEmployersCheck: Listed as preferred in many postings; checked through a GitHub notebook or an optional part of the take-home

skills.name: Data modeling basics and dbt: star schemas, fact/dimension tables, transformation layers
skills.howEmployersCheck: Interview questions on how you'd structure tables for a dashboard; dbt project in a portfolio. Increasingly expected at modern-data-stack companies

skills.name: Descriptive statistics and A/B test basics: significance, confidence intervals, cohort analysis
skills.howEmployersCheck: Conceptual interview questions; weighted more heavily for product-analytics roles

skills.name: Gathering requirements and prioritizing data requests from business stakeholders
skills.howEmployersCheck: Behavioral interview questions about handling ambiguous or competing requests

credentials.name: Bachelor's degree (any field; quantitative preferred)
credentials.note: Many postings list it, but demonstrated SQL and BI skill plus relevant experience often outweighs the field of study.

credentials.name: Tableau Desktop Specialist / Certified Data Analyst, Microsoft PL-300 (Power BI), or Looker certification
credentials.note: Occasionally a resume tiebreaker when a company uses that specific tool; rarely screened for.

credentials.name: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
credentials.note: Can show structured learning for a career changer but carries little weight with Bay Area hiring managers compared with a portfolio and SQL test performance.

proofOfSkill: A portfolio of 2-3 end-to-end SaaS-style analyses (e.g. funnel conversion, cohort retention/churn, marketing attribution), each with SQL queries, a published dashboard and a short written recommendation
A public Tableau Public / Looker Studio / Power BI dashboard built on a realistic B2B dataset, linked from the resume
A GitHub repo with well-commented SQL (CTEs and window functions), plus optionally a dbt project or Python notebook
Resume bullets describing past reporting work in terms of the business decision it drove and the metric it changed
Strong performance on the company's SQL screen and a clear walkthrough presentation of the take-home
caveats: The target doesn't state seniority. These requirements assume an entry-to-mid-level (Data Analyst I/II) role a career switcher would realistically target. Senior roles expect level-4 SQL, data modeling and stronger ownership of stakeholder relationships.

Titles vary widely. 'Marketing Analyst', 'Revenue/GTM Analyst', 'Business Intelligence Analyst' and 'Product Analyst' overlap with this role. GTM-focused roles weight CRM and attribution knowledge heavily, while product analytics roles weight experimentation and Python more.
The tool stack differs by company: Looker and Tableau are common, but Sigma, Mode, Hex and Power BI all appear. Snowflake/BigQuery with dbt is common but not universal. Check individual postings.
Bay Area interview loops often include a live SQL round and a case round. Smaller startups may substitute a take-home, and larger companies may add a stats round.
The 'analytics engineer' role is absorbing some modeling work, and expectations around dbt and AI-assisted querying are shifting quickly, so this snapshot may date.

profile.summary: This learner brings strong hands-on experience in marketing operations reporting, HubSpot data hygiene, and building/presenting attribution dashboards to leadership, giving her a solid foundation in data cleaning, spreadsheet modeling, storytelling, and SaaS marketing metrics. Her main gap is technical query and BI tooling: she has no SQL experience and hasn't used dedicated BI platforms, relying instead on Excel-based workarounds.

skills.evidence: Brief explicitly states she has no SQL or formal querying experience yet.
She builds attribution dashboards but only using Excel/HubSpot, with no mention of Tableau, Looker, Power BI, Mode or Sigma.
5 years in B2B SaaS marketing operations building attribution dashboards implies regular exposure to funnel and pipeline metrics, though CAC/LTV/retention aren't explicitly mentioned.

She builds attribution dashboards and weekly performance reports that require framing what to measure and how, though this has been within a marketing ops context rather than broader analytical scoping.
She owns HubSpot data hygiene including dedupe, field standards, and lead routing rules.
She presents attribution dashboards and campaign performance results at monthly marketing reviews to the VP of Marketing.
She builds weekly campaign performance reports using pivot tables and XLOOKUP.
She owns HubSpot data hygiene (dedupe, field standards, lead routing rules) and builds attribution dashboards from this CRM/marketing automation data.
No mention of any cloud data warehouse tool; her work has been entirely in Excel and HubSpot.
No mention of Python, pandas, or notebooks anywhere in her background, which is centered on Excel and HubSpot.
No exposure to data warehousing or transformation layers is mentioned; her work has been in spreadsheets and a CRM tool, not modeled databases.
Building attribution dashboards implies some comparative analysis, but there's no mention of formal A/B testing, significance testing, or cohort analysis.
She builds reports and dashboards specifically for the VP of Marketing and presents at monthly reviews, implying she gathers and responds to stakeholder reporting needs.

otherStrengths: 5 years of domain fluency in B2B SaaS marketing operations at a 400-employee company, which will help her frame relevant analytical questions.
Experience owning and standardizing data governance processes (field standards, lead routing rules) that translates to disciplined, careful analytical work.
Demonstrated persistence in a technical, detail-oriented individual contributor role over several years despite it not being a traditional analyst title.
